question: Inside each layer of `src/vs`, code is split into folders by the environment it runs in. What are those environments, and what may code in each one import?

points.text: `browser` (web APIs such as the DOM; may use `common`)
`electron-browser` (browser APIs plus a small IPC subset to the Electron main process; may use `common` and `browser`)

answer:
Inside each layer of `src/vs`, code is split into six environment folders. This comes from `.github/instructions/source-code-organization.instructions.md` and the `local/code-layering` rule in `eslint.config.js`. Both give the same table. Every environment may also import its own folder.

| Folder | Runs in | May import |
|---|---|---|
| `common` | Any environment, so only basic JavaScript | Only `common` |
| `browser` | Web or DOM environments | `common` |
| `node` | Node.js | `common` |
| `electron-browser` | The Electron renderer: browser APIs plus limited Electron IPC | `common`, `browser` |
| `electron-utility` | The Electron utility process | `common`, `node` |
| `electron-main` | The Electron main process | `common`, `node`, `electron-utility` |

Some consequences:
- `common` imports nothing environment-specific.
- `browser` and `node` are kept apart, so neither can import the other.
- `electron-browser` builds on `browser`, but it can't use `node`.
- `electron-main` is the widest. It sits on top of `node` and `electron-utility`, but it can't import `browser` or `electron-browser`.
- `electron-utility` can't import `electron-main`, so the dependency runs one way.

The layer rule is separate from this. Layers are ordered `base`, `platform`, `editor`, `workbench`, `code` / `server`, and `sessions`. A layer may only import from layers below it. For example, `editor` can't depend on `node` or `electron-*` code, and `workbench` must never import from `sessions`.

The layering rule is set to `warn` in the ESLint config, not `error`.
